_why: Escape-hatch ratchet: these counts may fall, never rise. Enforced by .claude/bin/escape-hatch-ratchet.sh at pre-commit and pre-pr. Raising a ceiling is a deliberate, reviewable edit to this file — see .claude/skills/_references/quality-gates.md Rule 4. Baseline measured 2026-07-30, BEFORE raising the lint set to strictTypeChecked (TASK-w3n8qr), because raising it is what produces new suppressions.

patterns.note: Never permitted: unlike @ts-expect-error it does not expire when the underlying error is fixed.
The sanctioned form, and there are none today. Ceiling 0 is not a ban: needing one means raising this to 1 with the reason, which is the reviewable act the rule asks for.
Covers the line, next-line and file-wide forms.

All 7 are in tests and all 7 are STRUCTURAL, not debt — the type system refusing the value is the thing under test, so the cast is the only way the test can exist. Draining this to 0 is not the goal; holding it at 7 is, and a cleanup ticket would invite work that cannot happen. Three feed deliberately invalid values to the validator (variant-input.validation.spec.ts: null as unknown as string, 'forty-two' as unknown as number). Three build a partial NestJS host or context that cannot be constructed for real in a unit test (app-exception.filter.spec.ts x2, request-log.interceptor.spec.ts). One hands the log emitter keys its type forbids, to prove they never reach the output line — the privacy rule of adr-request-observability-log, asserted rather than trusted (request-log.spec.ts). Raised from 5 on 2026-08-19 as a reviewable edit; the two new entries are the last two named.

_not_counted.non-null-assertion: No pattern for `x!` — the test files embed GraphQL documents, where `[VariantOrderInput!]` is GraphQL's own non-null syntax. Every candidate regex counted that as a TypeScript assertion. strictTypeChecked's no-non-null-assertion rule is the right owner (absolute, at the linter, per Rule 1), not a text-matching ratchet.
